The 2026-09-05 join-miss ruling (_decisions/2026-09-05_cad_join_miss_becomes_absent_verified.md) reaches landUse and does NOT reach zoningSource, because absence-of-row means absence-of-fact only when the source owns the fact.

entries: LESSON: BP-CONTENT-01 grades the SERVED payload, not the baked row, and the two are not the same artifact. facets.zoning is baked as a bare null on hundreds of thousands of rows and passes the walk only because attachVerdictLayersToFacets attaches a four-state first. Before deciding WHERE a required leaf's state belongs, ask which artifact the grader reads and where that leaf's answer actually becomes knowable -- a leaf whose state depends on parcel_record or city-limits containment cannot be earned at bake time at all.

LESSON: the dispatch's own write-path pointer can be wrong about the fifth leaf while being right about the first four, and the falsifier is what tells you. 16 of 16 live cohort failures involved zoningSource and 14 involved nothing else, so a bake-only reading of this dispatch would have produced a merged, tested, CI-green change that moved the cohort by one parcel.

LESSON: always split a per-county payload measurement by facetSchemaVersion before drawing a conclusion. The published table blended the live conformant writer with a retired 2026-07 one, and that blend accounted for every single 'absent key' -- a defect class the dispatch called 'separate and worse' that does not exist in the write path at all.

LESSON: hauska-factory's classifyRequiredLeaf passes ANY non-empty object whose verdict is not absent-verified/not-applicable/refused as {state:'value', ok:true}. Anything writing a leaf state that must be graded honestly has to map into those three words; writing the true-but-unrecognised verdict (lookup-failed, stamp-missing, unmeasured) makes the leaf read as POPULATED, which is worse than failing.

LESSON: `on: push: branches: [main]` in this repo's cloud-run-deploy.yml does NOT mean deploy-on-merge -- the push path runs build-and-push only, and every deploy job is workflow_dispatch-gated. Read the job `if:` conditions, not the workflow trigger, before deciding whether a merge is a customer-visible act.

DEAD-END: giving provenance.zoningSource a bake-side verdict. It looks defensible (the bake knows whether a stamp joined) and it is wrong twice over: the rail is decided later with more information, and on Elgin's declared-incomplete layer the only available bake-side answer is the absent-verified that a standing ruling forbids. Mirroring at the serve is the only shape that cannot disagree with the rail.

DEAD-END: writing a lookup-failed land-use absence at the leaf with its own verdict intact. It PASSES the walk -- as a value. Verified against the real classifier and left in the test suite as a standing assertion so nobody re-derives it as a clever shortcut.

DEAD-END: heredocs with apostrophes through this session's Bash tool. `cat > f <<'EOF'` aborts with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote' on any line containing an apostrophe, even though the delimiter is quoted. Write the file with the Write tool and `cat` it into place instead; cost two failed attempts.
